rationale: The assistant used the customer's evidence well (whole-dish variation, main fan oven only, knobs with neon) and asked a sensible question about neon cycling, with safe advice to avoid unattended cooking and leave thermostat work to an engineer. However it fixed on 'the main-oven thermostat is now the leading suspect' without ever proposing the cheap, decisive user checks the ground truth expects: an oven thermometer at a fixed setting, consistent preheating/shelf position, the door seal, the wobbly knob, or the model number. It repeated the fan-setting confirmation three times without the customer ever answering, and escalated to an engineer after only four exchanges, before any temperature measurement, so a homeowner could pay for a callout when user habits or a flattened seal might explain the variation. No parts were recommended and nothing was invented, so no critical failures apply.
